(distributed as a fixture subset inside the INFORMS Journal on Computing
code/data archive for Petris, Archetti, Cattaruzza, Ogier & Semet,
"A Branch-Price-and-Cut Algorithm for the Kidney Exchange Problem",
INFORMS Journal on Computing, 2025, DOI 10.1287/ijoc.2024.0664 / repo DOI
10.1287/ijoc.2024.0664.cd)

Named in KIDNEY_EXCHANGE_SCOPE.md's data plan as the "small, easy-to-version
fixture source" (as opposed to the full 437MB primary Petris et al. testbed,
DOI 10.57745/IHQAPY, not downloaded here).

License: MIT (confirmed directly from the fetched ORIGINAL_LICENSE file
above, and independently corroborated by the repo's own top-level
README.md, which states in its header: "This archive is distributed in
association with the INFORMS Journal on Computing under the MIT License.").

What this is: real kidney-exchange compatibility-graph instances from a
published, peer-reviewed operations-research paper ("Pansart et al. 2022",
introduced in arXiv:2201.08446 and reused as a benchmark by the Petris et
al. 2025 IJOC paper this repo accompanies). NOT randomly generated for this
project -- see ORIGINAL_DATA_README.md for the paper's own instance format
description (patient-donor pair count P, altruistic donor count N, max
cycle length K, max chain length L, and an (N+P) x P medical-benefit
matrix, -1 meaning "transplant not feasible").

What this is NOT: real hospital ownership. Pair-to-hospital assignment is
not part of this file format at all (it is a pure compatibility-graph
benchmark, no institutional/ownership metadata) -- see
`witness/kidney_real_data.py`'s module docstring for the declared synthetic
partition rule applied on top of this real graph, and
KIDNEY_EXCHANGE_SCOPE.md's "Data plan and evidence boundary" table, which
states this explicitly for exactly this reason.

Restrictions on use noticed: none beyond MIT-license attribution.

Not downloaded (out of scope for this project's two-way-only, no-chains
model, and not needed): `Pansart2022/Instances_Pansart2022.zip` (a nested
zip inside the fetched archive containing what appear to be additional/
alternate-format instance files) and the four alternate max-chain-length
(`l3`/`l6`/`l12`) variants per (P, N) combination beyond the one used by
`parsed.py` -- this project's model has no chains at all (see
`witness/kidney.py`'s module docstring), so L is irrelevant to which
variant is used; `parsed.py` reads the `_l3_0` instance for each (P, N)
pair (arbitrary among the L-variants, since L doesn't affect our model, and
replicate index 0 among the 5 available per (P, N, K, L) combination).
